# DropdownMenu

Generated from the spec. This page is a reference to the contract, not usage guidance.

A button that opens a list of actions or choices. Use it for commands and settings, not for site navigation or for picking a form value.

Stage: **alpha**. Figma: `Dropdown` (mapping not yet confirmed against the Components file). Behaviour: `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu`.

## Keyboard

Pattern: [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: Menu Button, opening a Menu](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/). Name: The trigger: its label, or with an icon-only Button its ariaLabel. The content is named by the trigger through aria-labelledby, which Radix sets. Each item is named by its label alone; an item with a description is labelled by its itemLabel and described by its itemDescription, which the adapter links. Each group and radio group is named by its label through aria-labelledby, which the adapter sets because Radix's Label is a plain div with no link to its group.

| Key | Part | Does | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enter | trigger | Opens the menu and highlights the first enabled item; on an open menu's trigger it closes the menu. | `dropdown-menu-trigger-enter-opens` |
| Space | trigger | Same as Enter. | `dropdown-menu-trigger-space-opens` |
| ArrowDown | trigger | Opens the menu and highlights the first enabled item. ArrowUp on the trigger does nothing; the menu-button pattern lists it as optional and Radix leaves it out. | `dropdown-menu-trigger-arrowdown-opens` |
| ArrowDown | content | Highlights the next enabled item. On the last item it stays put unless content.loop is true. With focus on the content itself, after a pointer open, it highlights the first enabled item. | `dropdown-menu-arrowdown-next` |
| ArrowUp | content | Highlights the previous enabled item. On the first item it stays put unless content.loop is true. With focus on the content itself it highlights the last enabled item. | `dropdown-menu-arrowup-previous` |
| Home | content | Highlights the first enabled item. PageUp does the same. | `dropdown-menu-home-first` |
| End | content | Highlights the last enabled item. PageDown does the same. | `dropdown-menu-end-last` |
| Enter | item | Chooses the highlighted item: runs its action, toggles a checkbox item or picks a radio item, then closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. | `dropdown-menu-enter-selects` |
| Space | item | Same as Enter, including on checkbox and radio items, where the pattern would keep the menu open. While a type-ahead search is in progress, Space is part of the search instead. | `dropdown-menu-space-selects` |
| Escape | content | Closes the menu without choosing anything and returns focus to the trigger. | `dropdown-menu-escape-closes` |
| Tab | content | Does nothing: Radix cancels it and focus stays on the highlighted item. The pattern says Tab closes the menu and moves on; Souvenir keeps Radix's behaviour. | `dropdown-menu-tab-held` |
| type-ahead | content | Typing printable characters highlights the next enabled item whose label starts with them. Typed characters build one search for one second. Repeating a single letter steps through the items that start with it. | `dropdown-menu-type-ahead` |

| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-attributes` | The trigger has aria-haspopup set to menu, aria-expanded set to true or false to match the menu, and aria-controls naming the content while it is open. | `test:dropdown-menu-trigger-attributes` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-one-button` | With a Button as trigger, asChild is set, so the page holds one button element and never a button inside a button. | `axe:nested-interactive` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-content-named` | The content has role menu and aria-labelledby pointing at the trigger's id. | `test:dropdown-menu-content-named` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-structure` | The content and every group in it hold only menu items, groups and separators as their owned children. | `axe:aria-required-children` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-item-parent` | Every menu item, checkbox item and radio item sits inside the content or a group inside it. | `axe:aria-required-parent` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-item-name` | Every action item has an accessible name from its label. | `axe:aria-command-name` | 4.1.2 |

| MUST | `dropdown-menu-description-not-name` | An item of any kind with a description has aria-labelledby pointing at its itemLabel and aria-describedby pointing at its itemDescription, so its accessible name is the label alone; type-ahead matches the label and never the description. | `test:dropdown-menu-description-not-name` | 4.1.2 |

| MUST | `dropdown-menu-checked-state` | aria-checked on every checkbox and radio item matches its checked value, and exactly one radio item in a radio group with a value is checked. | `test:dropdown-menu-checked-state` | 4.1.2 |

| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-space-opens` | Space on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused. | `test:dropdown-menu-trigger-space-opens` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-trigger-arrowdown-opens` | ArrowDown on the closed trigger opens the menu with the first enabled item highlighted and focused. | `test:dropdown-menu-trigger-arrowdown-opens` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-arrowdown-next` | ArrowDown moves the highlight to the next enabled item, skips disabled items, and stays on the last item while content.loop is false. | `test:dropdown-menu-arrowdown-next` | 2.1.1 |

| MUST | `dropdown-menu-home-first` | Home and PageUp move the highlight to the first enabled item. | `test:dropdown-menu-home-first` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-end-last` | End and PageDown move the highlight to the last enabled item. | `test:dropdown-menu-end-last` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-enter-selects` | Enter on a highlighted item calls its handler once, closes the menu and focuses the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-enter-selects` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-space-selects` | Space on a highlighted item calls its handler once, closes the menu and focuses the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-space-selects` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-escape-closes` | Escape closes the menu without calling any item's handler and focuses the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-escape-closes` | 2.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-tab-held` | Tab inside the open menu leaves focus on the highlighted item and the menu open, as Radix does. A change to close on Tab, as the pattern describes, must change this test first. | `test:dropdown-menu-tab-held` | 2.1.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-type-ahead` | Typing the first letters of an enabled item's label highlights it; disabled items are never matched. | `test:dropdown-menu-type-ahead` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-focus-returns` | After the menu closes by Escape or by choosing an item, focus is on the trigger. | `test:dropdown-menu-focus-returns` | 2.4.3 |

| MUST | `dropdown-menu-disabled-inert` | A disabled item has aria-disabled true, cannot be highlighted by arrow keys, type-ahead or the mouse, and pressing it calls no handler and leaves the menu open. | `test:dropdown-menu-disabled-inert` |  |

A checked checkbox or radio item shows its check mark or dot, never only a colour. | `test:dropdown-menu-highlight-not-colour-alone` | 1.4.1 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-text-contrast` | Every label, description, group label and shortcut hint has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against its background, highlighted or not, in every variant, in light and dark. Disabled items are exempt. | `test:dropdown-menu-text-contrast` | 1.4.3 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-forced-colors-highlight` | With forced colours on, the highlighted item shows an outline at least 2 pixels thick and the others show none. | `test:dropdown-menu-forced-colors-highlight` | 2.4.7 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-target-size` | Every item is at least 24 pixels tall and as wide as the content. | `test:dropdown-menu-target-size` | 2.5.8 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-item-layout` | Each item lays out in one row, in reading order: the indicator box or iconStart, then a column holding the label with the description under it, then iconEnd, then the shortcut hint at the end edge. The label column takes the remaining width, the icons and indicator box never shrink, and the shortcut does not wrap. The extensions stylesheet writes this. | `test:dropdown-menu-item-layout` | 1.3.2 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-label-wraps` | A label or description too long for one line wraps inside the item, which grows taller and keeps its padding; it is never cut off or hidden behind the shortcut. | `test:dropdown-menu-label-wraps` | 1.4.10 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-separator-line` | The separator is one line, 1 pixel (width/sm) thick, in border/primary/default, across the content's inner width, drawn on its block-start edge only, with space above and below it. The extensions stylesheet writes the one-sided border, the zero height and the space. | `test:dropdown-menu-separator-line` |  |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-fits-viewport` | At 320 pixels wide the open content lies wholly inside the viewport, at least content.collisionPadding from each edge, and no page scrolls sideways. Because menu/max (320) is wider than the 304 pixels left inside the padding, the extensions stylesheet also caps the width at --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-width. | `test:dropdown-menu-fits-viewport` | 1.4.10 |
| MUST | `dropdown-menu-scrolls-when-tall` | Content taller than the space Radix reports as available is capped at that height and scrolls inside itself, so every item can be reached on a short phone screen. | MUST | `dropdown-menu-modal-blocks-page` | While open with modal true, the rest of the page is hidden from assistive technology, does not scroll and ignores presses; a press outside closes the menu. | `test:dropdown-menu-modal-blocks-page` |  |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-shortcut-exposed` | An item with a shortcut hint carries the same shortcut in aria-keyshortcuts. | `test:dropdown-menu-shortcut-exposed` |  |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-touch-target` | Where the pointer is coarse every item is at least 44 pixels tall. (pattern) | `test:dropdown-menu-touch-target` |  |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-danger-not-colour-alone` | An item with variant danger names what it destroys in its label, such as Delete chat, because red alone does not tell everyone that the action is destructive. (pattern) | `manual:dropdown-menu-danger-not-colour-alone` | 1.4.1 |
| SHOULD | `dropdown-menu-right-item-kind` | A choice of one from several uses a radio group, an independent on or off setting uses a checkbox item, and only commands use plain items, so the checked state is announced. (pattern) | `manual:dropdown-menu-right-item-kind` | 4.1.2 |

Whether people expect this in Souvenir's menus is untested. (assumption) | `manual:dropdown-menu-checkbox-stays-open` |  |

## Content rules

- Item labels are short and start with a verb for actions: Rename chat, not Chat renaming.
- Checkbox and radio item labels name the setting or the choice, not the act of choosing: Extended thinking, Standard.
- A description is one short sentence that adds what the label cannot, such as Best for long documents. Leave it out when the label says enough.
- Group labels are short nouns, such as Models. Leave a label out when the items speak for themselves.
- Sentence case. No full stop in labels. An ellipsis only when the item opens a further step that asks for more, such as Rename….
- A danger item names what it destroys and sits last, after a separator.
- Shortcut hints use the platform's symbols, such as ⌘C on Apple devices and Ctrl+C elsewhere, and only for shortcuts that work.

## What the spec does not carry

- The live Figma components: their properties were read from a cached copy inside the Semantic Tokens file, which is older than the published library, so every figma mapping here is unconfirmed. In that copy Dropdown, the menu surface, is a plain component with the booleans showGroups and showDivider and no state property; both booleans are design-tool switches with no prop in code. DropdownItem has state (default, hover, selected, focus, disabled; default default), type (initial, danger; default initial), the text properties title and description, and the instance swaps prefix and suffix with the switches showPrefix and showSuffix, which have no prop in code. Figma's hover and focus are one state in code, [data-highlighted]; selected is [data-state="checked"] on a checkbox or radio item.
- The word for a destructive action differs: the Figma property is type with the value danger, and the tokens are the error tokens. The prop follows Figma's value under the name item.variant, because type means the element type in code; the styles use text/error, interactive/error/default and text/on.
- Layout written in the extensions stylesheet: the item as one row (indicator box or iconStart, a label column with the description under the label, iconEnd, then the shortcut pinned to the end edge), with the label column growing and the icons and indicator box not shrinking; white-space nowrap on the shortcut; the content's maximum height from --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height with vertical overflow auto; the content's width capped at --radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-width; the separator as a block-start border only, with no height and space above and below it. The requirements dropdown-menu-item-layout, dropdown-menu-separator-line, dropdown-menu-fits-viewport and dropdown-menu-scrolls-when-tall pin each of these.
- Submenus: Radix's Sub, SubTrigger and SubContent are left out. A menu that needs a second level should become a dialog or a page.
- Radix's Arrow part, which points at the trigger.
- Context menus opened by right-click, which are a different Radix package.
- The indeterminate checked state that Radix accepts for checkbox items.
- Icons and shortcut hints on checkbox and radio items: their start is the indicator box, and Figma's prefix and suffix are read here as belonging to action items.
- Any Radix Content prop not listed here, such as alignOffset, avoidCollisions, sticky and hideWhenDetached; they pass through unchanged at Radix's defaults.
- Enter and exit animation. Radix keeps the content mounted with data-state closed while an animation runs, but the spec format has no opacity or transform token, so none is specified.
- The trigger's look, which belongs to the Button spec, including how the chevron turns.
- The rest of the model selector fixes in the UI fixes tracker, such as how the Effort setting works.
